front.title: Content Stitching for Media over QUIC

abstract.t: Media over QUIC Transport (MOQT) requires that an Object is always the same bytes, no matter who asks for it or where it is retrieved from. That property is what makes MOQT content cacheable by relays. It also means that when different subscribers need to receive different content, the straightforward approach is to publish a separate track for each of them, even when most of what those tracks carry is the same. This document describes content stitching: building the tracks that subscribers receive out of Objects taken from other tracks, so shared Objects can be cached once while each audience still receives a track of its own. It names the pieces involved, describes how they fit together, works through some examples, and draws a line between a stitcher and a relay. It does not define a format or mechanism for stitching.
